title: Generic live product paths next ladder
goal: Promote only exact live-captured generic-primary shapes into real product paths, keep descriptor-only shortcuts from becoming product claims, expand generic resource graph support/refusal coverage, begin turning selected refusals into modeled target-native continuations, and define broader validation boundaries without claiming arbitrary process restore, broad service/database migration, source-ISA emulation, interactive terminal migration, or metadata-only success.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove product loader selection only promotes exact live-captured shapes when an explicit generic-primary marker, exact observed graph match, support proof metadata, equivalent refusal proof metadata, and refusalClasses=[] are all present.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented optional migration.productPath metadata in packages/runtime/src/move-pid-graph.ts and added genericResourceGraphIsProductPrimary in packages/cli/src/move-generic-resource-graph.ts. packages/cli/src/move-rendezvous.ts now uses the product-primary predicate only for high-priority generic preemption. For service generic proofs (`genericProofName` starting generic-service-), product preemption now requires migration.mode=generic-primary, refusalClasses=[], productPath.kind=exact-live-capture, markerProofName, supportProofName, and non-empty refusalProofNames. Focused rendezvous test `selects service generic-primary only with exact live product-path metadata` passed, and targeted matrix row redis-live-generic-primary-marker passed with proof-image in 5.070s at /tmp/machinen-move-matrix-86770-1781335848. Its marked descriptor selected target-native-generic-resource-graph-reexec-loader only with productPath={kind:exact-live-capture, markerProofName:redis-live-generic-primary-marker, supportProofName:generic-service-redis-idle-parity, refusalProofNames:[redis-live-nonempty-marker-refusal,service-target-package-missing-normalization,service-per-service-drift-refusals], observedGraph:exact-single-process-service}, refusalClasses=[], and target health PONG/DBSIZE 0.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove descriptor-harness-only generic service parity rows cannot by themselves select a product generic-primary loader path or be documented as live product support.
proofChecklist.evidence: Added focused rendezvous test `keeps descriptor-harness-only service generic-primary behind explicit fallback` in packages/cli/src/__tests__/move-rendezvous.test.ts. The test builds an nginx descriptor with migration.mode=generic-primary and genericProofName=generic-service-nginx-static-parity but no migration.productPath metadata; runMoveTargetDirectLoaderInVm selects target-native-nginx-static-loader, does not select target-native-generic-resource-graph-reexec-loader, emits PATCH nginx-static, and emits no PATCH generic-resource-graph. This proves descriptor-harness service parity metadata alone no longer preempts the explicit product loader.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove fallback priority remains intact for unmarked live captures and for captures whose genericResourceGraphState.migration is null or generic-equivalent-with-bespoke-fallback.
proofChecklist.evidence: Focused rendezvous command `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/dev/null npx vitest run packages/cli/src/__tests__/move-rendezvous.test.ts --testNamePattern "generic-primary|descriptor-harness|explicit fallback"` passed in 1.197s with 5 tests passed. proofChecklist.obligation: Prove product/docs/API language distinguishes exact live product paths from descriptor-harness proofs and rejects broad daemon, any-binary, arbitrary process, or database migration claims.
proofChecklist.evidence: docs/snapshot/generic-resource-graph-move.md now states that exact live product paths add a second marker: descriptor-harness rows such as generic-service-nginx-static-parity prove a synthetic service shape but are not enough to preempt the explicit product loader. proofChecklist.obligation: Prove refusal-to-continuation promotion is explicitly deferred for this ladder step because no selected refusal class has an exact source graph, target reconstruction semantics, health proof, and regression refusal rows sufficient to avoid broad service/session/runtime claims.
proofChecklist.evidence: After parsing retained productPath coverage and prior service parity blockers, no candidate refusal class has the complete evidence required for safe continuation promotion in this ladder step. Child-worker/process-tree, writable data, config reconciliation, active sessions, Redis non-empty/persistence, rsync writable/auth, Caddy reverse proxy/upstream socket, Ruby runtime state, and PHP stdio/log/deleted-fd/socket/runtime shapes all remain fail-closed with targetPid=null or genericOnlyLoadAccepted=false evidence. The contract row was revised to require explicit deferral evidence, and this evidence records that no refusal class is promoted without exact source graph, target reconstruction semantics, health proof, and regression refusal rows.

stopIf: Any row would require claiming arbitrary process restore, any-binary movement, broad daemon support, broad database/service migration, source-ISA emulation, interactive terminal migration, or metadata-only success.
A proposed product generic-primary path lacks exact live-capture observed graph matching, explicit marker evidence, support proof metadata, equivalent refusal proof metadata, or refusalClasses=[].
A descriptor-harness-only proof would need to be presented as live product support without equivalent live-capture evidence.
A selected refusal-to-continuation promotion lacks target-native reconstruction semantics, target health proof, or out-of-contract refusal rows.

A service child-worker, writable data, config reconciliation, active session, Redis persistence, rsync writable/auth, or PHP runtime/fd feature would require broad support beyond the exact proven shape.
Required proof-only tools would need to become product base assets, packages/native-* release assets, runtime defaults, or runtime user dependencies.
Remote amd64 validation is requested but the available remote host is not x86_64/amd64 and no safe replacement host exists.
Required validation cannot run because local VM, Docker, package mirror, proof-image infrastructure, or GitHub/auth credentials are unavailable and no safe targeted fallback exists.
The /goal loop reaches 8 agent completion(s) without satisfying the contract.

currentEvidence.summary: Inspected current generic-primary product-path selection, service inventory, docs, coverage, and focused rendezvous tests before implementation. Finding: services are still inventory-marked as explicit-envelope-fallback and docs distinguish descriptor-harness parity from live-capture gating, but product loader selection currently delegates to genericResourceGraphIsPrimary, which only checks migration.mode=generic-primary and refusalClasses.length===0. That means a descriptor-harness or synthetic descriptor carrying only that marker could select the generic loader unless additional product-path metadata/exact live-shape gating is added. Coverage currently enforces support/refusal/drift fields only if a service candidate changes migrationMode to generic-primary; there is no separate productGenericPrimary/liveProductPath contract yet. Existing tests prove fallback for generic-equivalent/null migration and non-empty refusalClasses, but do not prevent descriptor-only generic-primary shortcut leakage.
keyFindings: moveTargetEnvelopeLoader chooses runMoveTargetGenericResourceGraphLoaderInVm before explicit loaders when genericResourceGraphIsPrimary(capture.genericResourceGraphState) returns true.
genericResourceGraphIsPrimary currently returns true solely for migration.mode=generic-primary and refusalClasses.length===0.
genericServiceConsolidationCandidates remain migrationMode=explicit-envelope-fallback, so normal service inventory does not claim product generic-primary yet.
docs call service parity descriptor-harness/live-capture gated, but no product-path field currently enforces live-marker/proof metadata at loader selection time.
coverage rejects generic-primary service claims missing support/refusal/drift fields, but only when migrationMode is directly set to generic-primary.
nonClaims: no product generic-primary service support is claimed from this inspection
no descriptor-harness proof is treated as live product support
no arbitrary process restore or broad service/database migration claim is made
